newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Islamists says they stay in government.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Islamists says they stay in government.

text.p: Turkey's ruling Islamists on Thursday vowed to stay in government despite mounting military-led pressure to step down in a row over religious activism.
"I believe the government has work to do and it will keep on doing it," Ahmet Tekdal, an assistant head of the Islam-based Welfare Party, told a news conference.
Istanbul shares fell 6.85 percent to 1,427 at the close of morning trade on worries that Prime Minister Necmettin Erbaklan's coalition was crumbling.
Two ministers from the secularist wing of the alliance are in open rebellion against Islamist Erbakan for his failure to implement an anti-Islamist crackdown demanded by the army.
A key Welfare MP has also criticised the prime minister for not giving in to the powerful military, in a rare break in party solidarity.

The military, which sees itself as the guardian of Turkey's strict secularist system, is expected to pressure the government to carry out its demands at a National Security Council meeting on Saturday.
